name.text: A point on the line AB

questiontext.text:
\(\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a}\) and \(\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}\). Give the position vector, in terms of \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\), of a point R that lies on the line AB [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]beyond B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]beyond A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]between A and B, nearer to A than to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]between A and B, nearer to B than to A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]beyond B, with AR more than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]beyond B, with AR less than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]beyond A, with AR longer than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]beyond A, with AR shorter than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]between A and B, less than a quarter of the way from A to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]between A and B, more than three quarters of the way from A to B[[/if]].

\(\overrightarrow{OR} =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
A point with position vector \(\lambda\mathbf{a} + \mu\mathbf{b}\) lies on the line AB exactly when \(\lambda + \mu = 1\). Then \(\overrightarrow{AR} = \mu\,\overrightarrow{AB}\): the point is between A and B when \(0 \lt \mu \lt 1\), beyond B when \(\mu \gt 1\) and beyond A when \(\mu \lt 0\). The size of \(\mu\) says how many times as long as AB the line AR is.

For a point [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]beyond B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]beyond A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]between A and B, nearer to A than to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]between A and B, nearer to B than to A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]beyond B, with AR more than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]beyond B, with AR less than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]beyond A, with AR longer than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]beyond A, with AR shorter than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]between A and B, less than a quarter of the way from A to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]between A and B, more than three quarters of the way from A to B[[/if]] the coefficient of \(\mathbf{b}\) must be [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]greater than 1[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]negative[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]between 0 and \(\dfrac{1}{2}\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]between \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) and 1[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]greater than 2[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]between 1 and 2[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]less than \(-1\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]between \(-1\) and 0[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]between 0 and \(\dfrac{1}{4}\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]between \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) and 1[[/if]]. One answer is \({@samp@}\); another is \({@alt@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Vectors II: a point on the line AB

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.6: Construct the position vector of a point on line AB in a given position, using coefficients that add to 1.

node.description: On AB in the position asked for

node.sans: is(la = 1 and mu = 0) or is(la = 0 and mu = 1)

truefeedback.text: That is A or B itself; give another point.
\({@la@} + [[if test="is(mu < 0)"]]({@mu@})[[else]]{@mu@}[[/if]] = {@la+mu@}\), not 1, so R is not on the line AB. Points on AB have coefficients that add to 1.

R is on the line AB, but \(\mu = {@mu@}\) puts it [[if test="is(mu > 1)"]]beyond B[[/if]][[if test="is(mu < 0)"]]beyond A[[/if]][[if test="is(mu = 1/2)"]]at the midpoint of AB[[/if]][[if test="is(mu > 0 and mu < 1 and mu # 1/2)"]]between A and B[[/if]], with \(\overrightarrow{AR} = {@mu@}\,\overrightarrow{AB}\). For a point [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]beyond B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]beyond A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]between A and B, nearer to A than to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]between A and B, nearer to B than to A[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]beyond B, with AR more than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]beyond B, with AR less than twice as long as AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]beyond A, with AR longer than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]beyond A, with AR shorter than AB[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]between A and B, less than a quarter of the way from A to B[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]between A and B, more than three quarters of the way from A to B[[/if]], the coefficient of \(\mathbf{b}\) must be [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]greater than 1[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]negative[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]between 0 and \(\dfrac{1}{2}\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]between \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) and 1[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]greater than 2[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]between 1 and 2[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]less than \(-1\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]between \(-1\) and 0[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]between 0 and \(\dfrac{1}{4}\)[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]between \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) and 1[[/if]].
